prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my scientific judgment is unchanged. B045 is a complete discovery chain: proglucagon processing and incretin physiology (Holst, Drucker), identification of the truncated active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), and demonstration in humans of insulinotropic and satiety effects, followed by therapies whose benefit has been confirmed in large independent outcome trials for glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Maturity is not in question, and the physiology of gut-pancreas-brain signalling opened by this work fits Physiology or Medicine. Keeping a single part with three names avoids the arbitrary exclusions that any two-part configuration would force under the three-person cap, and the citation can state the therapeutic outcome so that the drug-development story is acknowledged without awarding it.
statement.case_against: The weakness remains attribution. Four credited names meet three seats, so Knudsen, whose acylated analogues made liraglutide and semaglutide practical, is left out, and that exclusion is a judgement about what the prize is for and not something the science settles. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide form is contested and Habener is outside the credited names; the supplied materials do not let me resolve this, and my recollection of the priority details is unverified. A prize may also be read as celebrating a commercially dominant therapy, and long-term safety and durability are still being studied.

responses.point: El-Manira moved from opening with Knudsen to the Mojsov trio, but argues that Knudsen's acylation strategy was a real mechanistic idea and that the citation should name the therapeutic outcome so the drug development is acknowledged.
responses.response: I agree that acylation to extend a half-life of minutes to days was a genuine conceptual step and not mere industry routine, and I agree the citation should name incretin-based treatment so the exclusion does not look like indifference to the therapy. I still keep Mojsov in the third seat, because the identification of the active peptide is the enabling scientific step on which every later agonist was built, and the Nobel precedent leans toward the discovery that opens a field. I do not read your acceptance as a reason to reopen the seat unless the committee concludes that Mojsov's claim cannot be defended.

responses.point: Linnarsson says the committee should check the primary literature on the active truncated peptide before the final ballot and would revisit the trio if Mojsov's claim proved weaker than assumed, and that a priority dispute does not make a contribution less real.
responses.response: I share the view that doubt should not decide the seat by default, and that a contested priority is not the same as no contribution. I have not verified the primary literature and do not claim to have settled it from the supplied record. My working position is that the identification and synthesis of the active form is a real and distinct contribution, so I retain Mojsov. I would change only if concrete evidence showed that the active-form finding belongs primarily to someone outside the credited names, in which case a pair of Holst and Drucker, with a citation worded on physiology, would be my answer and not a developer swap.

responses.point: Perlmann ties the Knudsen question to precedent, arguing that the committee leans toward discovery over development, and would change only if the citation must explicitly cover the drugs, in which case Knudsen would replace Mojsov and the choice should be stated openly.
responses.response: I agree that the choice should be made openly and I accept your framing. My answer is that this citation covers physiology and the active peptide, so the third seat goes to identification and not to design. I also take your point that B003 is credible but not better than B045. On the chair's question about B003 as a fallback, I rank it first, but the Zhou history and the parallel VLP groups mean the Lowy and Schiller core is firmer than the Queensland credit, and I would want that stated if it ever became the lead.

responses.point: Sandberg says the unfolded protein response B015 has the cleanest attribution on the list and would support HPV as a second prize in a future year, or this year if GLP-1 is not carried.
responses.response: I agree that Walter and Mori is the cleanest pairing on the shortlist and that the mechanism is textbook. I still weigh B015 below B045 because its disease relevance is prospective whereas B045 has both mechanism and demonstrated human benefit. On the chair's two-part question, I reconsidered a B045 pair plus B015 and rejected it: reducing B045 to two names would drop either Mojsov or the physiology core, and that is a worse cost than a single three-name part. I would keep B015 as a genuine fallback and a strong future candidate.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the committee rewards physiology and discovery alone or also translation, and how the citation can acknowledge Knudsen if she is not a laureate; he also treats B003 as the principal alternative.
responses.response: I would reward the physiology and the active peptide, with the therapy named as the consequence, and I think the citation wording I give does this. I share your view that the priority issues for B003 are real but that zur Hausen's 2008 prize covers the aetiology and not VLP vaccine design, so it does not count heavily against novelty. I agree B003 is the principal alternative and not a second part, since adding it to a three-person B045 would exceed the cap. Like you, I regard the Mojsov-Habener question as my main remaining uncertainty.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide is secure enough, given that Habener is outside the credited names; I could not verify this from the supplied materials.
Whether the committee accepts omitting Knudsen, and whether the citation wording is enough to acknowledge long-acting analogue design.
Whether B003 or B015 is the better fallback if B045 cannot be settled on attribution; I lean to B003 but its Queensland credit is not clean.
Long-term safety and durability of GLP-1 therapies are still under study, and I have not independently verified trial data.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal. My work on autoimmunity, Sjogren's disease and Ro52/TRIM21 is not on this shortlist, and I have no documented connection to any credited name on B045, B003 or B015. Shared Karolinska Institutet or committee settings do not constitute a personal tie.
